choices.text: Choose Lakeshore Club, with a pool and gym but no hot tub, a 23-minute event commute, and the strongest restaurant options nearby.
Choose Fulton House, with a pool and gym but no hot tub, a reliable 14-minute event commute, and fewer nearby late-night restaurants.
Choose Venue Suites, with a gym but no pool or hot tub, a 6-minute walk from the event, and a $90 higher total.
Choose North River Hotel, with a pool, gym, and hot tub, a traffic-sensitive 29-minute event commute, and lively dining on its block.

candidate.difficulty_rationale: Fulton House and North River offer balanced but different advantages: commute reliability versus a fuller recreation bundle and better dining. Generic reasoning cannot determine how Priya weights that extra amenity against repeated winter travel, but her history can.
candidate.gold_action: Select Fulton House, retaining the two durable facilities while avoiding a materially less reliable evening commute for the sake of a hot tub.
candidate.label_rationale: Fulton House satisfies the durable amenity preference in the applicable shared-stay scope. The Minneapolis evidence shows that a hot tub can settle a close choice but should not compromise commute quality, and the Scottsdale exception confirms that its absence can be accepted when stronger trip concerns prevail.
candidate.query: Priya and her spouse need four nights in Chicago around a winter professional event that ends late each evening. They expect to use the hotel during the day, but Priya also wants a manageable return after the event. All quoted rates are flexible and within budget. Which hotel should the planner select?

choices.text: Reserve Crescent Spa for $1,280 prepaid; it has a pool, gym, and hot tub, is closest to the French Quarter, and can offer only a Sunday treatment.
Reserve Garden Court for $1,340 flexible; it has a pool, gym, and hot tub, but its Saturday treatment is at 8:00 a.m. and it is a 20-minute ride from evening plans.
Reserve Canal Athletic Hotel for $1,190 flexible; it has a gym and hot tub but no pool, with a Saturday 2:00 p.m. treatment and the shortest airport ride.
Reserve Marigny House for $1,300 flexible; it has a pool and gym but no hot tub, with a Saturday 2:30 p.m. treatment and a central location.

candidate.difficulty_rationale: Garden Court and Marigny House are both flexible and provide the durable amenity pair; Garden Court adds a hot tub, while Marigny has the substantially better treatment time and location. The query alone leaves those benefits genuinely comparable, while history establishes which feature is softer.
candidate.gold_action: Reserve Marigny House, relaxing the additional hot-tub preference to preserve flexibility, the useful treatment time, location, and both durable facilities.
candidate.label_rationale: The Scottsdale evidence supports a trip-specific relaxation of the hot-tub preference when cancellation exposure and a confirmed treatment matter more, without revising the durable preference for a pool and gym. Marigny House matches that pattern in a new decision.
candidate.query: Priya and her spouse are booking three nights in New Orleans while waiting to learn whether her spouse's leave dates will shift. They also want a Saturday couples treatment, and every option meets their room and accessibility needs. Which booking best fits Priya's established decision pattern?

choices.text: Move to Harbor Exchange for $720; it has a pool and on-site gym but no hot tub, and the move takes about 35 minutes door to door.
Move to Beacon Spa Hotel for $790; it has a pool, gym, and hot tub, but adds 25 minutes to both planned dinner trips.
Keep the conference hotel for $690; it has an on-site gym but no pool or hot tub, avoiding the Friday move entirely.
Move to Public Garden Inn for $700; it has a gym and hot tub but no pool, and is a short walk from both dinners.

candidate.difficulty_rationale: Keeping the room is cheaper and avoids disruption, while moving yields the amenity pattern Priya repeatedly values during shared leisure stays. A planner must transfer the policy only to the extension rather than treating the entire mixed-purpose trip as uniformly in or out of scope.
candidate.gold_action: Move to Harbor Exchange for the leisure extension because the spouse's arrival changes the stay into the scope where preserving both durable facilities outweighs a moderate one-time move.
candidate.label_rationale: The preference did not drive Priya's solo work stay in the Raleigh evidence, but it does apply once the trip becomes shared leisure time with her spouse. Harbor Exchange satisfies the durable pair without the repeated location penalty or added cost of Beacon Spa Hotel.
candidate.query: Priya will spend three nights alone at a Boston conference, after which her spouse will join her for a two-night leisure extension. She may either keep the conference room or move hotels Friday afternoon; rates below are totals for the extension, and all options have similar cancellation terms and room quality. What should the planner arrange for the extension?

choices.text: Accept Cliff House at $1,440, with a pool and hot tub but no on-site exercise room; a public gym is 12 minutes away by taxi.
Accept Laurel Bay at $1,460, with a pool and on-site fitness center but no hot tub.
Accept Terrace Athletic at $1,420, with an on-site fitness center and hot tub but no pool.
Accept Atlantic Grand at $1,635, with a pool, on-site fitness center, and hot tub, plus a $60 dining credit.

candidate.difficulty_rationale: Laurel Bay offers lower cost while Atlantic Grand offers the complete recreation package and a credit, leaving a credible generic value tradeoff. Longitudinal evidence is needed to establish that the incremental feature is not worth this premium.
candidate.gold_action: Accept Laurel Bay because it provides the durable amenity pair at a competitive rate; the hot tub does not justify Atlantic Grand's substantial net premium.
candidate.label_rationale: Laurel Bay matches Priya's durable shared-leisure preference. Atlantic Grand's extra feature is favorable but secondary, consistent with her refusal to pay a large premium solely for a better recreation configuration in Puerto Rico and her use of a hot tub only as a close-choice tiebreaker in Minneapolis.
candidate.query: Priya and her spouse are comparing four six-night Madeira hotels. They expect several quiet afternoons at the property, and all four have equivalent views, breakfast, cancellation terms, and access to their planned hikes. Which quote should the planner accept?

choices.text: Book Sound Resort for $410; it has a pool, gym, and hot tub, with a 22-minute light-rail trip to the audit office.
Book Market Athletic for $430; it has a gym but no pool or hot tub, with a 14-minute bus ride and several restaurants nearby.
Book Ledger Hotel for $445; it has no recreation facilities, with a covered 7-minute walk to the audit office and cancellation until arrival day.
Book Lake Union Club for $395 prepaid; it has a pool and gym but no hot tub, with a traffic-sensitive 18- to 30-minute ride.

candidate.difficulty_rationale: Sound Resort is cheaper and offers a strong poor-weather evening option, while Ledger Hotel offers commute reliability and flexibility. Without the historical scope boundary, either is defensible; with it, applying the shared-leisure policy to Sound Resort would be an overgeneralization.
candidate.gold_action: Book Ledger Hotel because this short solo work stay falls outside the established shared-leisure scope, so its reliable covered commute and flexibility should decide the comparison rather than recreation facilities.
candidate.label_rationale: The Raleigh evidence explicitly distinguishes solo work stays from stays with Priya's spouse and records that recreation amenities should not drive the former. Ledger Hotel therefore wins on trip-relevant logistics even though it lacks the facilities favored in another scope.
candidate.query: Priya is traveling alone for a two-night Seattle compliance audit with 7:00 a.m. starts. She will have one free evening, the weather forecast is poor, and all four hotels meet the audit's security and expense rules. Which should the planner book?

choices.text: Choose Lakeshore Club for $1,090, with a pool and on-site gym but no hot tub, a 24-minute train trip to the event, and the widest choice of nearby restaurants.
Choose Fulton House for $1,160, with a pool and on-site gym but no hot tub, a predictable 14-minute shuttle trip to the event, and limited late-night dining nearby.
Choose Venue Suites for $1,080, with an on-site gym but no pool or hot tub, a covered 6-minute walk from the event, and a daily breakfast credit.
Choose North River Hotel for $1,120, with a pool, on-site gym, and hot tub, a traffic-sensitive 25- to 35-minute ride to the event, and several late-night restaurants on its block.

candidate.difficulty_rationale: Fulton House and North River Hotel present a genuine tradeoff between a shorter predictable return and a lower-priced hotel with a hot tub and better late dining. The current trip facts do not assign a decisive weight to those benefits; Priya's longitudinal policy makes the hot tub secondary to preserving the core pair without accepting a materially worse repeated commute.
candidate.gold_action: Select Fulton House, preserving both durable recreation facilities while favoring the predictable evening return over North River Hotel's additional hot tub and dining advantages.
candidate.label_rationale: The Raleigh evidence establishes that shared stays with Priya's spouse call for both a pool and a fitness facility. The Minneapolis episode shows that a hot tub is only a close-choice benefit and should not compromise the commute, while the Scottsdale exception confirms that the hot tub may be relaxed when a stronger trip concern matters more. Fulton House therefore fits her policy better than North River Hotel despite the latter's lower price, complete recreation bundle, and better dining.
candidate.query: Priya and her spouse need four nights in Chicago for a winter professional event that ends at 10:30 p.m. each evening. Their afternoons are uncommitted, and all four hotels have suitable rooms, flexible rates, and practical transit connections. Which hotel should the planner select?
